name: principle-subtract-before-you-add
purpose: Remove obsolete behavior and redundant complexity before adding its replacement, then build on the simpler base.
triggers: Sequencing an addition, refactor or rewrite
Removing dead code, redundant validators or stub references
outputs: Removal before construction, simpler prompts and references, and observed implementation checks when available
Ordered proposal with explicit limits when writes or execution are unavailable
ordinaryExample: Inspect callers of an obsolete handler, remove that handler and its redundant validator, then add the specified replacement without speculative guards.
capabilityLimits: Removal requires source and usage evidence, authorization and writes; checks require observed execution.
Missing writes or execution permit a reduced proposal; missing source blocks safety and completion claims.
Invocation metadata is preserved without assuming host enforcement.
Host behavior has not been tested.
